name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,502

clue.text: Bid completed by telephone

blocks.note: a call is a bid in card games such as bridge
as in 'time is up': finished, over

explanation.surface: An auction bid finalised over the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bidding by phone at an auction; the definition is the last word and the phrase CALL UP is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone on the phone is to call them up, a common phrasal verb.

clue.text: Fellow penning work about old lift system

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word for work is read from its end
a fellow penning something holds it inside, as a pen encloses animals

blocks.note: a man's name standing for any fellow
OP is short for opus, a work
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A man writing a piece about an antique elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' is British for an elevator, which the surface leans on, but here it means a ride in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car pool commuters share rides, and a ride given is called a lift in British English.

clue.text: Confine some Gujarati militants on the way back

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are wanted, a run inside them
travelling back means the letters run in the opposite direction, upward in a down entry

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Restraining a group of militants from Gujarat as they return.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict or confine it within bounds; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Not easy to understand French article on Settle

blocks.note: un is the French masculine indefinite article, 'a'
to settle a debt is to clear it

explanation.surface: An obscure French article written about the Yorkshire town of Settle.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire, which is why it has a capital; here it is simply the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear is obscure or confusing, hard for a reader to grasp.

clue.text: Next to island retreat owned by old scholar

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the word for island is turned round
something owned by another is held in its keeping, here held inside it

blocks.note: the Venerable Bede, an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian
IS is an abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island hideaway belonging to an ancient scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside is a preposition meaning alongside or at the side of something.

clue.text: Book by Thackeray primarily set in town

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the novelist's name counts
a thing set in somewhere is placed inside it

blocks.note: Esher is a town in Surrey
the novelist's initial

explanation.surface: A novel by Thackeray with its setting in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Thackeray novel, but the book is from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is one of the books of the Old Testament, telling of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: Made up of parts from books found inside? That's fantastic I say

indicators.note: something found inside another sits within it
I say signals that what has been built is spoken, and the answer is the word it sounds like

blocks.note: i.e., that is
New Testament, a set of books
great as an exclamation of delight

explanation.surface: Something assembled from components of books, with a delighted exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: I(NT)E GREAT said out loud is INTEGRATE. The answer is used in its rare adjective sense.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, integrate is an old word for composed of separate elements, whole and complete.

clue.text: Catch up, absorbed in abridged record of informal alliance

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for catch is written bottom to top
an abridged text has been cut short, so the final letter goes
something absorbed in another is taken inside it

blocks.note: to net is to catch
to enter details is to record them

explanation.surface: Catching up with a shortened account of a loose alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is an understanding between nations, short of a formal treaty, such as the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: In subjection and still tolerant

blocks.note: under someone's control
standing water is still

explanation.surface: A person who is oppressed yet remains forgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: An understanding person is sympathetic and forgiving, accepting others' faults.

clue.text: Leave quickly without son's stuff

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for a male child is taken away

blocks.note: scram is slang for go away fast
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone dashing off without their son's belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun, the son's things; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to pack or force tightly into a space, the same as to stuff.

clue.text: Form it with stone cut irregularly

indicators.note: done irregularly means not in the proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shaping something from roughly hewn stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To constitute a whole is to make it up or compose it, as parts form a whole.

clue.text: It's an expression of dissatisfaction with support in footwear

blocks.note: what a crowd shouts when displeased
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Complaining about the arch support in a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootee is a soft knitted boot for a baby, or a short boot, so it is a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Suddenly appearing to blend into space close to Bert

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space
to merge is to blend
the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Someone materialising and fading into the room near a man called Bert.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is half an em, a printing measure for the space a letter takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergent means coming into view or being born, newly arising.

clue.text: Fellow graduate kind, on reflection, to small bird

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the other way round

blocks.note: a man's name standing for any fellow
Bachelor of Arts
a sort is a kind
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A fellow graduate is, on reflection, kind to a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small bird' reads as a unit; small is wordplay and the bird is anything but small.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a large seabird of the southern oceans with a very long wingspan.

clue.text: Offhand about high quality description of most planes

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is placed round the second

blocks.note: an airy manner is casual and dismissive
worth is merit or excellence

explanation.surface: A casual remark about how good aircraft are.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fit and safe to fly is described as airworthy, which most are.

clue.text: Look for an expert on France

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so the expert follows the country

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Seeking a specialist on French matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look for' reads as a phrasal verb meaning seek; split it, and look is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A face, as in 'a sour face', is the expression or look someone wears.

clue.text: One dealt clubs and hearts essentially needing diamonds

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for the suit of clubs
the two central letters of the six
D is the abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A bridge hand where clubs and hearts call for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are what a dealer hands out, so a card is one item dealt in a game.

clue.text: Find guilty when new girl is discovered with Conservative in bed

indicators.note: the letters sit in the bed, enclosed by it

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
N is the abbreviation for new
Vi, short for Violet
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: a Tory MP caught in bed with a new girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: To convict is to declare someone guilty of a crime after a trial.

clue.text: Welsh soccer star describing those in attendance at Levante's opening game

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the star's name goes round the rest

blocks.note: Gareth Bale, the Welsh footballer
the gate is the number attending a match
the first letter of the Spanish club's name

explanation.surface: Gareth Bale talking about the crowd at a Levante home match.
explanation.walkthrough: Bale played in Spain for Real Madrid, so Levante fits the scene; a gate is a British term for a match crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game in which balls are struck into holes guarded by pins.

clue.text: Pilot bird endlessly seen on rocky peak

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: an avian is a bird
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A bird spotted on a craggy summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is someone who flies aircraft, a pilot, especially in early flying days.

clue.text: Sententiously brief American politician in charge after a bit of luck

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter
A is the abbreviation for American
Con is short for a Conservative
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A US politician whose post came through good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse, using very few words, like the Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Georgia has something to drink and a piece of upside-down cake

indicators.note: a piece of a word is a fragment of it, here its first letter

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a drink
its first letter

explanation.surface: A drink and a slice of upside-down cake in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upside-down' looks like a reversal signal, but it is just the source of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Not auspicious for peace keepers before conflict with Germany

blocks.note: the United Nations sends peacekeepers
as in 'ten to six', meaning before six
a war is a conflict
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A grim outlook for peacekeepers heading into war with Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfavourable or unfortunate, the opposite of promising or auspicious.

clue.text: Left complete with note in converted attic

definitions.note: a past participle phrase; intact describes the state of something left whole

indicators.note: a converted space has been remodelled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for note
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finding a note in a loft conversion that was left undisturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, nothing missing, as if left untouched.

clue.text: Starts to talk with Australian noting guttural local intonation

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

blocks.note: the initials of five words

explanation.surface: Chatting with an Australian about the throaty local accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a distinctive nasal quality of speech typical of a region's accent.

clue.text: Note to Kenneth destroyed after knight leaves to get married

indicators.note: when the knight leaves, his letter is taken away
something destroyed is broken up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: ti, also te, is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
taken as written
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A note to Kenneth torn up after a knight departs to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie the knot is an idiom for marrying, from the knot binding the couple.

clue.text: Girl stripping off somewhere in France

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer covering, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: the Riviera resort

explanation.surface: A girl undressing on a French beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannes, on the Riviera, is famous for its beaches as well as its film festival, which suits the stripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a girl's given name; crosswords use any name to stand for a girl.

clue.text: Go public in trial

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
once news is out it is public

explanation.surface: A plan to go public partway through a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go public' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryout is a test of a person or thing to see whether it is suitable.

clue.text: Disastrous for soldier trapped in overturned vehicle

indicators.note: an overturned vehicle is upside down, so its word is read backwards
something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: a cart is a vehicle
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier pinned under an upturned vehicle, a calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic means calamitous or dreadfully unfortunate, causing great suffering.
